title: Integrated compliance evidence workflow: RBAC, logging, retention, and incident-secure SDLC
author: Asha R. Kapoor
body:
Overview:

This playbook defines a single, auditable workflow for collecting, retaining, and packaging compliance evidence spanning RBAC and authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC controls, and incident-response security artifacts. Its goal is to reduce variance during audits (SOC2/ISO/PCI reviews), accelerate evidence production, and codify acceptable risk/exception processes.

Scope:
- Applies to Redwood production and staging services, identity providers, logging pipelines, CI/CD systems, and customer-facing control plane components.
- Does NOT replace service-specific runbooks; it standardizes the evidence lifecycle and exception handling across the security surface.

Primary owners and contacts:
- Evidence curator (primary): security-compliance@redwood.com
- RBAC owner: infra-identity@redwood.com
- Logging & retention owner: observability@redwood.com
- Secure SDLC owner: eng-platform@redwood.com
- Incident packaging lead: incident-coord@redwood.com

High-level lifecycle (steps):
1) Trigger identification: audit request, internal control test, or incident.
2) Scope mapping: list affected services, environments, and control IDs (see Control ID Schema v1.2).
3) Evidence collection: collect RBAC snapshots, auth configs, log extracts, change approvals, and CI/CD artifacts.
4) Sanitize & redact: apply data residency filters (per region) and PII redaction rules.
5) Package & sign: produce a timebound evidence package with manifest and cryptographic signature.
6) Store & share: publish package to the evidence archive and provide reviewers with secure link and access.
7) Close & retain: update retention metadata and schedule deletion or escalated retention if required.

Detailed procedures

A. RBAC & Authentication snapshot (owner: infra-identity)
- What to capture:
  - Principal list for the target environment: user/service principal/role names, origin (SSO / service account), last-used timestamp.
  - Effective permissions map for the target resource (ACLs/policy binds).
  - Policy change history for the last 90 days: git commits, PRs, approval logs.
  - SSO configuration snapshot (IdP metadata URL, SAML cert thumbprint, SCIM sync status, MFA enrollment policy).

- How to capture (commands / locations):
  - Identity service: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $(vault read -field=token secret/infrabot)" "https://idp.internal.redwood.com/api/v1/principals?env=prod" > rbac-principals.json
  - IAM policies: export from infra-git: git fetch && git log -p --since="90 days" infra/iam > iam-policy-changes.patch
  - Access logs: query audit-log index: kuery: "event.type:policy.change AND @timestamp:[now-90d TO now]"

- Output artifact names: rbac-snapshot-<service>-<YYYYMMDD>.json, rbac-policy-history-<service>.patch

B. Audit logging extraction & retention (owner: observability)
- Logged sources to include:
  - API gateway request/response metadata (non-PII),
  - Authentication events (login, token-issue, token-revoke),
  - Policy evaluation events (allow/deny),
  - Config change events from gitops pipelines,
  - KMS/Key access logs for crypto operations.

- Retention schedule (default):
  - Security audit logs: 7 years (encrypted at rest, index withheld for 1 year then archived).
  - High-fidelity debug traces: 90 days.
  - Access logs (web/API): 365 days.
  - CI/CD pipeline artifacts: 2 years for release artifacts; build logs 180 days.

- Query example:
  - ElasticSearch/Kibana: GET /_search?q=service:gateway AND event.type:auth &range=2024-01-01..2024-12-31

- Packaging guidance:
  - Export at most the minimum timeframe that satisfies the auditor's request. Use selectors: service, trace_id, user_id.
  - When cross-region data residency constraints apply, extract logs only from region-specific log stores and mark the package with region tag (e.g., eu-west-1).

C. Data residency & retention filtering (owner: observability / legal)
- Rules:
  - PII must be removed or redacted before moving outside the region declared by the customer/data classification.
  - Evidence packages can be regionally bound; when an auditor offsite requires access, use a secure review session (Zoom + screen share + ephemeral viewer) unless explicit consent to export region data exists.

- Redaction checklist:
  1. Identify PII fields by schema (users table: email, phone, ip).
  2. Mask emails: user@example.com -> u***@example.com (keep domain for context).
  3. Remove full request bodies that contain customer content unless explicitly requested and approved by legal.

D. Secure SDLC artifacts required (owner: eng-platform)
- Required evidence for a change control review:
  - PR/commit history for the change (link + patch),
  - CI run results including dependency scans, SBOM snapshot for the release, unit/integration test summary,
  - Deployment approval record (canary/rollout policy), release notes, and rollback plan,
  - Security code review checklists and remediation tickets closed.

- Example artifact names: sdlc-pr-<id>.patch, sbom-<release-id>.json, ci-results-<build-id>.tar.gz

E. Incident response security artifacts (owner: incident-coord)
- Triggered when the workflow is started for a security incident. Additional artifacts:
  - Incident timeline (IOC list, start/end timestamps, actors),
  - Forensic disk/network captures (hashes and storage locations),
  - Triage notes and escalation approvals,
  - Post-incident writeup and action items (RCA).

- Packaging constraints:
  - Forensic artifacts must be sealed (checksummed) and stored in the Forensic Vault (s3://redwood-forensics/<incident-id>/) with restricted ACLs.
  - Access to sealed artifacts requires justification and approval by the CISO or stamped delegate.

F. Evidence packaging and signature
- Manifest format (manifest.json):
  - fields: package_id, created_by, created_at, controls_covered (list), artifacts (list of artifact entry objects), region_tag, retention_until, signature (sha256).
- Signing process:
  1) Compute SHA256 digest of each artifact, record in manifest.
  2) Sign manifest with compliance signing key (stored in HSM).
  3) Store package as tar.gz and upload to evidence archive with encrypted metadata.

G. Archive storage and access controls
- Archive location: s3://redwood-evidence-archive/<year>/<package_id>/ (encrypted with CMK-evidence).
- Access policy: only security-compliance, SOC-reviewers, and legal group have read access; requests by others via evidence-request workflow.
- Audit trail: every download request generates a download event logged to audit-index: evidence.downloads (retained 7 years).

H. Risk and exceptions process (owner: security)
- Types of exceptions:
  - Short-term operational exceptions (<=30 days): e.g., retention not available due to migration. Requires risk-ack ticket and approval from security manager.
  - Long-term exceptions (>30 days): requires risk assessment, compensating controls, and Director-level approval.

- Exception request template (ticket must include):
  - Control impacted, justification, duration requested, compensating controls, rollback plan, owner, and business impact assessment.

- Approval workflow:
  1) Submit ticket to security-risk queue.
  2) Security reviews for compensating controls.
  3) If >30 days or PII-sensitive, escalate to Legal & CISO for sign-off.
  4) Record in exceptions register (exceptions-register.csv) and attach to package if relevant.

I. Evidence production SLOs and quality checks
- SLOs:
  - Initial packaged evidence delivery for standard audit requests: 5 business days.
  - Incident-related evidence bundles (high-priority): 48 hours initial package, full package within 14 days.
- Quality checks:
  - Each package must include a manifest, redaction checklist, and a reviewer sign-off (security + owner team).

J. Playbook examples (quick runbooks)
- Standard audit request (SOC2):
  1) Security triage: assign package id and curator.
  2) Run RBAC export command for the affected services.
  3) Pull log slices using timeframe and service filters.
  4) Sanitize using data-residency script: python tools/redact.py --region eu-west-1 --input logs.json --output logs.redacted.json
  5) Generate manifest and sign.
  6) Upload and notify auditor via secure link.

- Incident evidence bundle (short form):
  1) Run incident-collect.sh <incident-id> which queries idp, logging, and infra-git.
  2) Seal artifacts with sha256sum and upload to s3://redwood-forensics/<incident-id>/.
  3) Notify CISO and Legal with package metadata.

K. Templates and scripts (locations)
- Redaction scripts: git@repo:redwood/security-tools.git:/tools/redact.py
- Evidence manifest template: git@repo:redwood/security-compliance.git:/templates/manifest.json.tpl
- Incident collection tool: s3://internal-tools/bin/incident-collect.sh (versioned)

L. Compliance evidence review checklist
- Checklist items to tick before release:
  - [ ] Manifest present and signed
  - [ ] RBAC snapshot included
  - [ ] Required logging slices present
  - [ ] SDLC artifacts attached where relevant
  - [ ] Region & PII redaction applied per policy
  - [ ] Reviewer approvals recorded

Related controls and references
- Control catalog: Control ID Schema v1.2 (link internal).
- RBAC standard: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/rbac-guidelines-2024
- Logging architecture: /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/log-collection-architecture-2023
- Retention schedule: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/retention-schedule-2024

Appendix: example manifest (text)
{
  "package_id": "pkg-20251107-az3",
  "created_by": "asha.kapoor@redwood.com",
  "created_at": "2025-11-07T14:32:00Z",
  "controls_covered": ["RBAC-1", "LOG-2", "SDLC-3"],
  "artifacts": ["rbac-snapshot-serviceX-20251107.json", "logs-serviceX-20251107.redacted.json"],
  "region_tag": "eu-west-1",
  "retention_until": "2032-11-07",
  "signature": "sha256:..."
}

Contact and escalation
- For immediate concerns: pager on-call via Ops channel (#security-oncall).
- For audit scheduling and long-term requests: security-compliance@redwood.com
